articles.title: Two female leopards sterilised in India's first such initiative - Down To Earth
articles.content: In a first, the Junnar forest division in Pune district of Maharashtra has launched a scientific study to control leopard fertility through immunocontraception—a non-lethal method of population management. According to a press statement issued by forest officials, two female leopards have been administered the immunocontraceptive vaccine and safely released back into the wild. Immunocontraception involves administering a vaccine that triggers an immune response, temporarily enabling an animal to become infertile. It is a long-term, but not permanent, protection against pregnancy. Unlike permanent sterilisation, the method offers a reversible means of controlling reproduction. The study has received formal approval from the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. Human-leopard conflict became a prominent issue during Maharashtra’s state elections in 2024, particularly in the densely farmed, sugarcane-growing areas of Pune district. In talukas such as Junnar, Ambegaon, Shirur and Khed, candidates pledged to take measures to reduce conflict if elected. Between 2000 and 2025, leopard attacks killed 56 people in the Junnar forest division alone. The pilot project follows a directive issued in August 2025 by Sudhir Mungantiwar, then Maharashtra’s forest minister, instructing the forest department to prepare an action plan for leopard sterilisation. In April 2026, the department selected five female leopards for observation. The field operations are being conducted by frontline staff of the Junnar forest division, with an emphasis on safety, minimising trauma and providing veterinary care, according to the press statement. RESQ Charitable Trust, a wildlife rescue and rehabilitation organisation, is providing veterinary expertise and on-the-ground support. The Indian Council of Medical Research in Mumbai is also participating in the study. Researchers will analyse blood samples to monitor hormonal changes and assess the vaccine’s longer-term effects on the leopards, officials said. The pilot aims to establish whether immunocontraception is a feasible, safe and effective tool for managing leopard populations in high-density areas such as Junnar. The state forest department will monitor the animals throughout the study, the statement added. Leopards are classified as “endangered” under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. The Convention on International Trade of Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES) also lists the animal under the Appendix I category, implying it is at risk of extinction.

articles.title: Aaka Space plans india's first underwater human spaceflight analog mission in Gujarat
articles.content: BENGALURU: Private sector companies are working overtime to build and testIndia’s first underwater human space flight analog mission. A two-part analog mission has been planned by Aaka Space. The first, which is a trial running for 24 hours, will be done in December in a controlled environment in Gujarat. The second of 72-hour duration will be conducted in March 2027, for which the location is yet to be finalised. Aaka Space had earlier conducted the Ladakh Human Analog Mission. “The underwater mission aims to create a high-fidelity habitat capable of simulating several operational, physiological and psychological challenges associated with human spaceflight. As India advances toward crewed missions through Indian Space Research Organisation’s (ISRO) Gaganyaan programme and future long-duration habitation ambitions through Bharatiya Antariksh Station, the need for advanced astronaut training environments and human-performance research platforms is becoming increasingly significant,” said Astha Jhala, Founder and CEO, Aaka Space. Underwater environments are considered to be the closest to outer space analogs. Inside underwater habitats, astronauts experience isolation, confinement, dependence on engineered life-support systems, restricted mobility, altered spatial orientation and operational risk. These conditions are similar to what astronauts face in spacecraft and in space. The tests will also help the upcoming Samudrayaan mission. Apart from partnering with ISRO, an agreement will also be signed with the Indian Navy for the mission. Underwater habitat studies have shown that confined environments can influence cardiovascular function, respiratory response, fatigue, stress, sleep cycles and cognitive performance – particularly when atmospheric conditions such as elevated carbon dioxide accumulation are not effectively controlled. By combining underwater engineering with human spaceflight analog research, the initiative signals the emergence of a new generation of extreme-environment research infrastructure in India.
